correctness.rationale: For all fields, the horizontal projection U and central intersection K of an ideal satisfy [U,A+B]=P tensor B + A tensor Q subset K. Conversely every such K and linear lift define precisely one ideal. Goursat classification of U by P,Q,A0,B0 and a quotient isomorphism yields the count; the quotient dimension M, Grassmannian E choices and Hom(U,Z/K) count give the remaining factors. Smooth relative Grassmann and GL_c/affine bundles prove geometric strata. Seven exhaustive direct-bracket RREF checks confirm the finite arithmetic and include all 417199 subspaces of F2^8. The center equals A tensor B, and ad(x)^2=0 forces every one-dimensional ideal to be central, proving the enumerator-rigidity corollary.

value.rationale: All k-linear Lie ideals in the natural complete-bipartite graph Lie algebras constitute a motivated structural invariant. The exact all-dimensional finite-field census and geometrically irreducible smooth Goursat strata extend beyond graph-supported special ideals and require non-coordinate quotient-isomorphism parameters; K_{2,2} over F2 has a nontrivial total of 247 ideals. The family is infinite in part sizes and uniform in field characteristic, not an arbitrary isolated computation. The full ideal-dimension enumerator also determines the unordered bipartition sizes: its degree recovers p+r+pr and its linear coefficient recovers pr from the center-line count, so the family is distinguished by the invariant.
